In Table U4, the most restrictive criteria are removed for siting data centers, and because of this the vast majority of the state has considerable viability for the technology. The only exceptions include Salt Lake, David, and Weber counties. These fall into a small region of the state impacted by floodplains and high seismic activity. All three also share portions of the Great Salt Lake, further reducing suitability. As previously established, suitability for reactors in the state of Utah is for the most part patchy, and this is duly reflected in the collocation maps in Table U5. Here it is more evident that the higher slope tolerance for the water-cooled SMR technology allows for more contiguous regions of collocation suitability, though the lack of cooling water requirement
